options.en: The % at each point in the year needs to be calculated and the profits apportioned as accurately as possible
An average % for the year can be taken
The profit should be split equally among all partners at the end of the tax year
The profit should be split equally among all partners during the year
The partnership pays the profit, not the individuals

explanation.en: The correct answer is A. The percentage needs to be fully reflected at each point for each partner in their own self-assessment.

stem: Susan has begun work at the beginning of the tax year and then becomes ill and goes down to part-time hours. By the end of the year, she has earned £5,000. She paid some PAYE in April as she earned more that month than any other month.
ask: Which of the following best describes Susan's position now?

options.en: Nothing needs to change
She should not declare the first month of salary in the next year to even it up
She can reclaim the PAYE paid as she is below the threshold for paying income tax in the year
She should have been paying PAYE throughout, so tax is likely to be due
Susan cannot reclaim the PAYE paid, but is entitled to a tax credit in the next tax year

explanation.en: The best answer is C. As Susan shouldn't have paid any income tax, it is likely that she will have a refund for amounts already paid.

stem: A self-employed individual is able to include expenses against their income in order to establish their final taxable income.
ask: Which of the following best describes expenses they would be able to claim for?

options.en: Stationery for personal use
The entire heating bills at home if the person is working from home
Interest on a loan for school fees
A proportion of the heating bills at home if the person is working from home
Food whilst travelling on the road

explanation.en: The correct answer is D. To be reclaimable, an expense has to be incurred wholly and exclusively in the course of business. Food is not necessarily deductible because the individual would have had to eat, regardless.

stem: Sean operates his own private clinic in Harley Street and is employed part-time in an NHS hospital. Sean asks you to explain what National Insurance liabilities might be incurred.
ask: Which of the following best describes Sean's National Insurance obligations?

options.en: If Sean does not pay NI he will not get NHS treatment
Sean cannot vote if he does not pay NI
NI is automatically taken from everyone who works, regardless of age
NI depends on the amount Sean earns, whether he is employed or self-employed
NI has no bearing on Sean's entitlement to state pension

explanation.en: The correct answer is D. NI is taken from those who are under the pensionable age at a rate appropriate to their earnings. It does affect entitlement to some state benefits including pensions, but does not impact on entitlement to NHS treatment directly.

stem: An individual is keen to reduce their income tax bill and asks you about the various allowances they have heard other people mentioning. The individual in question is a single person who has never been married nor had children. They are employed and do not incur any self-employed based expenses or have any business related loans.
ask: Which of the following best describes a relief that may be available to him?

options.en: Maintenance payment relief
Married person's allowance
Pension contribution
Deductible expenses
Interest on a qualifying loan

explanation.en: The correct answer is C. If they are paying towards a recognisable pension scheme, this may be deductible. All other reliefs may generally be available, depending on the facts, but not as the facts are listed here.

stem: The tax year does not run from the 1st of January to the 31st of January in any given year. Your client comes into your office with several different receipts that he wishes to include as part of his expenses for self-employed income from various dates. You are preparing the accounts for the year 2016-2017.
ask: Which of the following best describes dated invoices which you would be able to include in the accounts?

options.en: An invoice dated the 10th of April 2016
An invoice dated the 10th of March 2016
An invoice dated the 31st of December 2017
An invoice dated the 1st of January 2016
An invoice dated the 10th of April 2017

explanation.en: The correct answer is A. The tax year 2016-2017 runs from the 6th of April 2016 to the 5th of April 2017.

stem: You are consulted by a software start-up business. They have started trading but have not decided what business structure to adopt and how to divide profits. You explain that the way in which income tax is payable to HMRC varies, depending on the situations of the individuals in question. You are asked to explain the various different ways payments are made.
ask: Which of the following best describes the options available to the clients?

options.en: If the staff are both employed and self-employed, they don't need to fill in a self- assessment
If the staff are only employed, it is possible to pay income tax through self-assessment by regular direct debit
Self-employed people pay tax through PAYE, deducted by the business before they receive their pay
Employees will not be able to make adjustments at the end of the tax year if their situation has changed and they become self-employed
If the staff are both employed and self-employed, they still need to fill in a self- assessment

explanation.en: The correct answer is E. Someone who is self-employed and employed will still have to do a self-assessment for their self-employed portion of income.

stem: A man has two loans. One is a mortgage on his house and the other is a loan for mechanical equipment at the plant he owns. He believes interest payments can be deducted from his income tax bill.
ask: Advise the man regarding the current legal position?

options.en: Interest payments are never tax deductible
Only the interest payments for mortgages are tax deductible
Interest payments are only tax deductible if the loan is a qualifying loan
Interest payments are only tax deductible if the loan is from the government
Interest payments are only tax deductible if the loan is for a fixed asset

explanation.en: The correct answer is C. In order for interest payments to reduce one's income tax bill the loan in question must be a 'qualifying loan'. A qualifying loan is normally a loan which is taken out to buy shares in the borrower's company or buy part of a partnership. A qualifying loan can also include loans to buy machinery, but does not generally include loans to buy property for personal use. In this instance, it is likely that the man's interest payment on the loan for the mechanical equipment would reduce his income tax bill, but his interest payments on his mortgage would not.

stem: A person believes that, as a sole trader, he is still entitled to the personal tax free allowance but his friend says this is incorrect.
ask: Advise the person regarding the correct legal position?

options.en: Sole traders do not pay income tax
Sole traders pay income tax but are not entitled to the personal tax free allowance
Sole traders are only entitled to the tax free personal allowance if their annual income does not exceed £50,000
Sole traders pay income tax and are entitled to the personal tax free allowance
Sole traders do not pay income tax, but must pay Corporation Tax on all profits

explanation.en: The correct answer is D. Sole traders do pay income tax, but they are entitled to the personal tax free allowance.

stem: A woman is self-employed and pays income tax on her income. She maintains the source of the income is irrelevant but a friend says she is wrong.
ask: Advise the woman regarding the current legal position?

options.en: Income tax rates differ depending on the type of business a sole trader operates
Rates of income tax are the same regardless of the type of income
Income tax only applies to savings income
Income is split into different categories in order to determine the tax rate
Income tax only applies to non-savings income

explanation.en: The correct answer is D. When discussing income tax, income can be split into three categories; non-savings income (e.g. from work, pension etc.), savings income and income from dividends. The rate of income tax paid on savings and dividend income is calculated after the non-savings income is calculated and the rate will depend on the amount of non- savings income a person has.

stem: Your client thinks that funds from property can never be subject to income tax, but her friend disagrees.
ask: Which of the following best describes the current legal position?

options.en: Funds from property are always subject to income tax
Funds from property are always subject to capital gains tax
Funds from property are always subject to income and capital gains tax
Funds from property can be subject to income tax
Funds from property are never subject to income tax

explanation.en: The correct answer is D. Income from property (and investments) can be subject to income tax.

stem: A woman is an employee in a hardware shop. Throughout the year her employer gives her £200 and £300 as bonuses because he is pleased with her work. As these payments are bonuses, the woman assumes they are not part of her taxable income.
ask: Advise the woman regarding the current legal position?

options.en: Bonuses are not considered as a taxable income
Bonuses of up to £500 a year are not considered as a taxable income
The bonuses are part of the woman's taxable income
Bonuses of up to £750 a year are not considered as a taxable income
Only part of the bonuses will be considered as the woman's taxable income

explanation.en: The correct answer is C. Money received from an employer in return for work is considered taxable income, as are any perks or benefits received.

stem: Your client comes to speak to you about his taxation position. He tells you that he is employed part-time and also works as a freelancer on a regular basis.
ask: What would represent the best advice to the client regarding his tax obligations?

options.en: Your client's employed income will be paid under self-assessment and his self- employed income will be paid under Pay As You Earn (PAYE)
Your client's employed income and his self-employed income will be paid under self- assessment
Your client's employed income and his self-employed income will be paid under PAYE
Your client's employed income and his self-employed income will be deducted 'at source'
Your client's employed income will be paid under PAYE and his self-employed income will be paid under self-assessment

explanation.en: The correct answer is E. Employed work is deducted at source under PAYE (formerly "Schedule E") and self-employed is calculated under self-assessment (formerly "Schedule D").

stem: A trainee solicitor has been assigned to the corporate tax department. She does not think that personal income tax matters are relevant to her role in the corporate tax department, which appears to only deal with businesses.
ask: Which of the following statements best advises the trainee?

options.en: Corporations deal exclusively with corporate tax issues; income tax is irrelevant
Income tax is only relevant where the owners and directors are the same people
Income tax is payable on salaries, but is also relevant to partnership shares
Income tax is part of payroll and is of no real concern to companies
Income tax is a separate regime to the corporate tax regime and they are mutually exclusive

explanation.en: The correct answer is C. Income tax is payable by partners on their partnership share and also potentially needs to be considered when it comes to the amount of tax paid by the directors overall. C is the most correct answer, as it is paid on employed income and partnership shares even though it does have an indirect impact on corporations as well.

stem: It is coming to the end of the tax year and the tax department of a business is busy dealing with income tax returns. A member of the department has split the clients between those that are employed and those that are self-employed. She is unsure, however, what the differences are between these two categories.
ask: Which option offers the best advice to the woman?

options.en: Self-employed individuals pay their tax on a monthly basis
Employed individuals pay their tax on a monthly basis
Self-employed individuals have tax deducted 'at source'
Self-employed individuals are taxed under self-assessment
Self-employed individuals are taxed under 'Pay As You Earn' (PAYE)

explanation.en: The correct answer is D. Self-employed individuals pay tax under self-assessment (formerly "Schedule D"). Although employed individuals will often pay their tax monthly it is the direct deduction before receiving their salary that is crucial.

stem: Your client is sorting out a variety of issues relating to their taxation position and is looking for ways to reduce the amount of tax they pay. Your client is particularly concerned with reducing the amount of National Insurance (NI) that he pays and asks you what the purpose of this tax is and how it applies.
ask: Which of the following is the most accurate and complete response that you could give to his concerns?

options.en: If your client is self-employed he does not have to pay NI contributions, but if employed he will have to
The amount of NI contribution that is due will depend entirely on whether or not your client is employed or self-employed
The amount of NI contribution that is due will depend entirely on the income of your client regardless of whether they are employed or self-employed
The amount of NI contribution to be paid is down to your client's preferences, but will impact on how much they get as a pension in the future and the benefits they are entitled to

The amount of NI contribution will depend on whether your client is employed or self- employed and the level of income that he has. The level of NI contributions will have an impact on benefits entitlement to some extent, but, primarily it is related to salary and employment status

explanation.en: The correct answer is E. The level of NI payments to be made depends on whether your client is self-employed or employed and the level of income. If someone has failed to pay the minimum NI contribution, they may find themselves with a reduced pension or benefits entitlement, but primarily, the level of contribution depends on salary and employment status.

stem: You are responsible for Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (FSMA) compliance in your firm. The firm are not authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA). You consider that some of the firm's work would, in any event, not require authorisation.
ask: Which of the following activities will not be regulated under the FSMA?

options.en: A solicitor who sells investments in his capacity as personal representative during the winding up of a client's estate
Buying shares on behalf of a corporate client
Advising on the merits of selling a particular investment
Making arrangements for a stockbroker to buy trusts on behalf of a probate client
A solicitor who prepares a will for a client who owns equities and trusts as part of their estate

explanation.en: (E) is correct - all the rest constitute regulated activities for solicitors: (A) dealing in investments as principal; (B) dealing in investments as agent; (C) advising on investments; (D) arranging a deal in investments. Preparing a will for the client to sign is not a regulated activity under the FSMA.

stem: You work for a large wills and probate firm. You are often asked by clients to advise about investment trusts. Having specialised in this area of law for many years, you have sufficient knowledge to provide the specific, detailed advice that your clients need.
ask: Which of the following exclusions are not likely to apply to you as a solicitor engaged in trust work?

options.en: The 'necessary' exclusion
The trustee exclusion
The 'absence of holding out' exclusion
The exclusion for giving generic advice only
The 'authorised third party' exclusion

explanation.en: The best answer is D. All the exclusions in (A) - (C) and (E) could apply where a member of the firm is a trustee. While generic advice (D) can be given, it is difficult to envisage a situation in which advice will be truly generic in trust work, as you are likely to be discussing particular investments in the estate. Therefore, (D) is the best answer.

stem: You are asked to advise clients with respect to protecting savings and corporate capital. In addition, you have discretion to oversee the day to day operation of clients' investment activities.
ask: Which of the following best describes the exclusion or exclusions from the RAO that is/are available to the regulated activities of 'safeguarding' and 'managing"?

options.en: The 'necessary' and 'body corporate' exclusions
The 'trustee/PR' exclusion
The 'ATP/execution-only client' and 'body corporate' exclusions
The 'trustee/PR' and 'body corporate' exclusions
All of the exclusions in the RAO are capable of applying to the regulated activities of 'safeguarding' and 'managing'

explanation.en: (B) is the best answer. The 'ATP' and 'body corporate' exclusions apply to all regulated activities, except for safeguarding and managing, therefore (C) and (D) are incorrect. It is not correct that all of the exclusions in the RAO are capable of applying to the regulated activities of 'safeguarding' and 'managing'. (E) is incorrect. The 'necessary' exclusion is available for most activities, including safeguarding but not for managing. Hence (A) is incorrect. The 'trustee/PR' exclusion is available for all activities, including safeguarding and managing. Therefore, (B) is correct.

stem: You are advising a software company in a takeover. Your client is looking to purchase a controlling interest in the target company. You are not authorized by the FCA. Where a corporate solicitor gives advice in connection with the purchase or sale of shares in a company,
ask: Which of the following best describes whether they can rely on the 'body corporate' exclusion?

options.en: The 'body corporate' exclusion will apply provided the shares carry 50% or more of the voting rights in the company
The 'body corporate' exclusion will not apply where the shares carry less than 50% of the voting rights in the company
The 'body corporate' exclusion will only apply to shares in public companies
The 'body corporate' exclusion will only apply to shares in private limited companies
The 'body corporate' exclusion will apply provided the shares are in a private company and they carry 50% or more of the voting rights in the private company

explanation.en: A is the best answer. (B) is incorrect, because the 'body corporate' exclusion may still apply even where the shares carry less than 50% of the voting rights in the company - where the object of the transaction is to transfer the day-to-day control of the company to the purchaser (for example, where the other shareholdings are fragmented). The exclusion will apply to any body corporate - and so includes shares in both public and private limited companies. Therefore (C), (D) and (E) are incorrect.

stem: Case A: You broker a litigation settlement for the specific performance of a contract in which your client agrees to purchase a certain number of shares in the other side's company. You then present the other party with a cheque on behalf of your client, draw up a stock transfer form and submit the completed form to the company secretary for registration of the transfer of ownership. Case B: You negotiate a settlement in a personal injury case in which your client will receive a lump-sum payment, and the client now seeks your advice on how best to invest the money.
ask: Which of the following statements best explains the legal position?

options.en: You can rely on the 'necessary' exclusion in both Case A and Case B
You can rely on the 'necessary' exclusion in Case A but not in Case B
You can rely on the 'necessary' exclusion only in Case B and not in Case A
In Case B, you could not refer your client to an authorised third person to obtain advice
The 'necessary' exclusion would not be appropriate in either of these Cases

explanation.en: (B) is the best answer. All of the arranging activities in Case A should reasonably be regarded as a necessary part of the litigation services. In Case B, however, the investment advice to the client, coming as it does after the client has already received the lump-sum payment, could not be regarded as comprising a necessary part of the litigation services provided by you (in which case you would have to rely on the Part XX 'incidental' exemption). (D) is incorrect. A solicitor can always obtain advice on behalf of a client from an Authorised Third Person (ATP), who gives the advice on a fully disclosed basis, because it will then be the ATP and not the solicitor who will be providing the advice (provided that he accounts to the client for any commission received from the ATP).

stem: You are the executor of a will for a longstanding client. The client and beneficiaries instructed you to provide investment services in winding up the estate in your capacity as trustee.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the trustee/PR exclusion?

options.en: The trustee/PR exclusion will not apply to a solicitor who is the executor of a will and who also provides investment services in winding up the estate in his capacity as trustee or PR, even if he receives no additional remuneration for so acting

A solicitor who is the executor of a will and who also provides investment services in winding up the estate in his capacity as trustee or PR may not charge for his activities as trustee/PR, even if the remuneration for the regulated activities is calculated by reference to the 'time spent' on such activities whilst doing his probate work
The cost for the time spent by the solicitor on any investment activities need not be included within the overall bill for the client and may be separately billed
The trustee/PR exclusion will only apply where the solicitor does not receive any remuneration from his client
The trustee/PR exclusion may apply even where the solicitor receives remuneration from his client

explanation.en: (E) is the correct answer. The trustee/PR exclusion will still apply when the solicitor is remunerated by his client for the regulated investment activities performed by him. The only condition that must be satisfied is that the solicitor must not receive remuneration for his work in addition to any remuneration he receives as trustee or PR. The investment work must not therefore be billed for separately - it must be included within the overall bill to the client for the trustee or PR services. However, the mere fact that the solicitor may spend an hour of his time on regulated activities whilst doing probate work and receive remuneration for such 'time spent' does not, of itself, mean that he is being 'additionally remunerated' for undertaking investment management duties.

stem: You are a partner in the corporate department of a large provincial firm. You have several corporate finance specialists who advise about transactions involving bonds, shares and other investment products. As the firm expands, investment advice becomes an increasingly important area of the firm's work.
ask: In respect of the Part XX exemption, which of the following statements best describes the legal position?

options.en: Where less than 50% of a firm's income is derived from investment business, the work will be incidental
No pecuniary reward must be received from any third party unless the solicitor has informed the client that the firm has received commission and has requested the client's permission to keep it
The investment activity must be part of the main legal services being provided by the solicitor
The solicitor must only account to the client for commission which exceeds £20
If the firm has a separate office, the exemption can be relied on provided that the investment activity is less than 50% of the firm's aggregate income

explanation.en: (C) is the best answer. The key test of Part XX is whether the activity is complementary to other professional services supplied by the firm, i.e. the activity must be done in connection with or as part of the main legal services being provided - eg. selling shares as part of winding up an estate. (A) will not always be correct - for example, if the firm has a separate department for providing financial services to clients or holds itself out as offering financial services assistance, the work may not be incidental, even if less than 50% of the firm's income is derived from investment business, but a separate activity in its own right. Therefore (E) is also incorrect. (B) is incorrect. 'Accounting to the client' does not simply mean telling the client that the firm will receive commission. It means that the client must be told unambiguously the precise amount of the reward and that the money belongs to the client. Only if the client then agrees that the firm can keep it will there have been full accounting. (D) The rule to account for the client for all commission received from third parties (found in both s. 327 FSMA and the Scope Rules) and 01.15 of the SRA Code of Conduct contain no de minimis for commission that must be accounted for to the client. Firms must therefore account for all commission received from a third party relating to a regulated investment activity regardless of its amount.

stem: In the process of providing estate planning advice to your client, you consider a variety of alternative investments. You do not have FCA authorization and are cautious about which investments you provide advice about.
ask: Which of the following best describes 'non-retail investment products'?

options.en: Term life insurance policies
Unit trusts
Personal pension schemes
Endowments
Investment trust savings schemes

explanation.en: (A) is the best answer. All the others constitute pre-retail investment products portfolios of investments

stem: You have a broad client base which includes large companies, small companies, sole traders, trustees and individuals. Under Rule 5(3) of the SRA Financial Services (Scope) Rules 2001, a solicitor must not advise a client to buy a security or relevant investment from a person whose business it is to buy and sell such investments.
ask: Which of the following best describes when this prohibition will apply?

options.en: Where the client is a corporate client who wishes to buy shares in a company
Where the client is an individual acting in the course of a business
Where the client is acting in his capacity as trustee of an occupational pension scheme
Where the client is a 'lay individual' client who requests advice on the purchase of debentures
Where a corporate client acts as trustee of an occupational pension scheme

explanation.en: Only (D) is the best answer. While the prohibition in Rule 5(3) of the Scope Rules would not apply in cases (A) - (C) and (E), it would apply to advising a 'lay individual' (i.e. non- company) client on the purchase of securities, such as debentures (being non-retail investment products).

stem: You are approached by a corporate client who asks you to safeguard, administer and manage their investments which consist of non-retail investment products. You recommend an authorized third party who can assist. The client seeks your advice about some of the investments that the ATP recommends, which you advise the client to avoid.
ask: Under the SRA Financial Services (Scope) Rules 2001, which of the following statements is true?

options.en: A firm may not safeguard and administer investments for a client
Discretionary investment management services are permitted under certain circumstances
A solicitor may not advise a client not to buy particular investments
A solicitor may not give advice to a corporate client regarding the purchase of a non- retail investment product
A firm may not safeguard and administer investments for a corporate client

explanation.en: (B) is the best answer. Discretionary investment management services maybe permitted - e.g. where a member of the firm acts a trustee/PR and, in addition, all routine management decisions are taken by an ATP, or any decision taken to enter into a transaction involving buying an investment is taken in accordance with the advice of an ATP. The SRA Financial Services (Scope) Rules 2001allow a firm to safeguard and administer investments for a client - therefore (A) and (E) are inaccurate. A solicitor may give a client negative advice - hence (C) is also inaccurate. Rule 5(3) permits advice to a corporate client in connection with the purchase of non-retail investment products - (D) is therefore also inaccurate.

stem: You are a partner in a busy high street practice carrying out the following types of work: (i) Assisting a client who is buying a house to find a suitable endowment mortgage, making arrangements for him to buy the policy recommended by the ATP and communicating with your client regarding the said policy. (ii) Advising a personal representative to sell assets of a deceased's estate which include shares. (iii) Acting as a trustee pursuant to the 'trustee/PR' exclusion under the RAO.
ask: Which of the following best describes whether these activities constitute an unlawful financial promotion?

options.en: Only assisting a client who is buying a house to find a suitable endowment mortgage, because no RAO exemption applies

Only advising a personal representative to sell assets of a deceased's estate which include shares, even if the trustee exemption applies, as the solicitor will still be subject to the financial promotion rules
Only making arrangements for the client to buy a policy recommended by an ATP, even though the ATP exemption applies, as the solicitor will still be subject to the financial promotion rules

Any assisting, making arrangements, advising or acting as a trustee, since) even where an exclusion under the RAO would otherwise apply to exclude an activity from FCA regulation (e.g. ATP or trustee exclusions) - the solicitor will still be subject to the financial promotion rules
The financial promotion rules would not apply where exclusion under the RAO would otherwise apply to exclude an activity from FCA regulation (e.g. ATP or trustee exclusions)

explanation.en: (D) is the best answer. All three activities would require FCA authorisation or an exemption from regulation. Even where an exclusion under the RAO would otherwise apply to exclude an activity from FCA regulation (e.g. ATP or trustee exclusions) - the solicitor will still be subject to the financial promotion rules.

stem: While the firm is carrying on incidental and complementary Part XX activities, you make unsolicited financial promotions during the course of a telephone conversation with a client. You then send out financial promotions, limited in content, by e-mail. You suggest to the client, when you next speak, that he may be interested in considering an introduction to an ATP. You finally call in order to introduce the client to the ATP.
ask: Which of the following best describes whether the restrictions on financial promotions will apply?

options.en: Unsolicited financial promotions made during the course of a telephone conversation with a client, where the firm is carrying on incidental and complementary Part XX activities will contravene the restrictions on financial promotions
Financial promotions sent out by e-mail, which are limited in content, will contravene the restrictions on financial promotions
A one-off financial promotion made by a solicitor suggesting to a client that he may be interested in considering an introduction to an ATP will contravene the restrictions on financial promotions
A communication made for the purpose of introducing a client to an ATP will contravene the restrictions on financial promotions

Firms are exempted from the restrictions on financial promotions where they carry out Part XX incidental and complementary activities; make solicited or unsolicited real- time promotions; non-real time financial promotions which are limited in content; one-off financial promotions; and introduce a client to an ATP

explanation.en: (E) is the best answer as all of the options A-D constitute independent (and unrelated) exemptions under the Financial Promotions Order. Financial promotions are exempted under the Financial Promotions Order, where firms carrying out Part XX incidental and complementary activities make solicited or unsolicited real-time (e.g. made in telephone conversation) promotions (A); non-real time financial promotions (e.g. e-mail which are limited in content (B); one-off financial promotions (C); and communications made for the purpose of introducing a client to an ATP (D). In all the cases mentioned, therefore, the financial promotions will be exempted.

stem: You represent an elderly client with respect to estate planning, drafting a will and minimizing likely Inheritance Tax costs. As you are not authorised by the FCA, you refer the client to an independent financial adviser (IFA), although you have knowledge and experience of investment options.
ask: If an IFA recommends a particular investment on behalf of a client, which of the following best describes your duties towards the client?

options.en: You must examine the IFA's recommendation and warn the client if the investment appears to be unsuitable
By referring the client to the IFA you have acted in your client's best interests, and no further obligations are therefore imposed on you
Only in the case of an appointed representative (tied agent) need you review the advice given
You must not examine the IFA's recommendation or warn the client if the investment appears to be unsuitable, as you are not authorised by the FCA to provide investment advice
An IFA may never recommend a particular investment on behalf of a third party

explanation.en: (A) is the best answer. According to mandatory principle 4 of the SRA Code of Conduct, you must always act in the client's best interests. Generally, a referral to a competent IFA cannot be criticised (hence (E) is incorrect). However, a client must always be warned against unsuitable investment activity even if recommended by an independent broker (and certainly if recommended by a tied agent, which sells the products of just the one product provider). Option (B) and (D) are therefore incorrect, and option (C) is only partially correct.

stem: You advise a client in respect of estate planning matters, and the client decides to take out a whole life policy. You refer the client to a suitable independent financial adviser (IFA), who provides competent advice. The IFA sends you £19.99 commission, which you inform the client about.
ask: Which of the following statements is the most accurate?

options.en: A solicitor does not need to account to his client for any commission that is less than £20 received from investment-related business
A solicitor must account to his client for any commission received from an IFA to whom he has referred his client under the introducing exclusion for arranging deals in investments
A solicitor does not need to account to his client for any commission below £20 received from an insurance company for general risk insurance to which the solicitor has referred the client
Any commission generated by a whole life policy must be accounted for to the client
Only commission above £20 generated by a whole life policy must be accounted for to the client

explanation.en: The best answer is (D). Any commission generated by a whole life policy must be accounted for to the client. 01.15 of the SRA Code of Conduct requires solicitors to account to their clients for any commission. Where a commission has been received from investment-related business, a solicitor must account for all commission received. Hence (A) and (E) are incorrect. Where a solicitor has received a commission from an IFA to which he has simply referred his client under the introducing exclusion for arranging deals in investments - this commission will be subject to rule 01.15. However, commission from any other sources, e.g. the insurance provider, must also be accounted for. Therefore, (B) is incorrect. Since general risk insurance does not contain any investment element, not being a security or a relevant investment, receipt of such commission is therefore subject to 01.15. (C) is therefore incorrect - any commission received needs be disclosed. In any event, for commission generated by a relevant investment (e.g. a whole life policy) regard must be had to the commission and accounting requirements of the RAO and the Scope Rules which also provide that all commission must be accounted for ((D) is therefore the correct answer).

stem: A solicitor refers a client to a financial advisor who is the appointed representative of a large bank to advise on the purchase of some unit trusts in a fund managed by the bank. The financial advisor intends to go ahead and purchase the trusts on the client's behalf.
ask: Which of the following best describes the regulatory position of the parties?

options.en: The financial advisor is permitted to purchase the trusts on the client's behalf as this will be a referral for independent advice
The financial advisor is permitted to purchase the trusts on the client's behalf as the appointed representative will be an exempt person
The financial advisor is permitted to purchase the trusts on the client's behalf because an introduction to an exempt person will always be excluded from the RAO
The solicitor will be in breach of mandatory principles, 01.2 and Chapter 6 of the SRA Code of Conduct 2011
The financial advisor is permitted to purchase the trusts on the client's behalf because an introduction to an appointed representative will generally be excluded from the RAO

explanation.en: (D) is the best answer. Mandatory principle 4, 01.2 and the objectives in Chapter 6 will have been breached by not acting in the client's best interests. IB6.2 requires a solicitor to inform the client before referring to a financial advisor who can only offer products from one source, which does not seem to have happened here. Note that an introduction to an exempt person will generally be excluded from the RAO; however, in the case of an appointed representative, this exclusion will not apply because a tied agent cannot give independent advice (which is one of the conditions for the introducing exclusion to apply).

stem: You represent your client who is purchasing a flat. The client asks you for advice about mortgages and about the best option for repaying the mortgage to maximise the equity in the property over time. He then asks if you can manage the mortgage policy chosen.
ask: Which of the following will not constitute regulated activities under the RAO in the field of conveyancing?

options.en: Arranging an endowment-linked (life policy) mortgage for a client
Obtaining advice for a client on which life or pension policy is most suitable
Managing a client's regulated mortgage policy
Administering a client's regulated mortgage policy
Arranging a pension fund mortgage for a client

explanation.en: The best answer is C. Regulated mortgage contracts, although listed as a specified investment under the Act, are neither securities nor relevant investments and, therefore, the activities of dealing, arranging, managing, safeguarding and advising will only apply to them to the extent that these are specifically prohibited by the RAO. According to the RAO, mortgages must not be "arranged, entered into as lender, recommended or administered." Advising on or making arrangements in respect of mortgages where an endowment policy or pension policy is to be used as additional security, or entering into an RMC as a lender, will thus all be caught by the Act. Managing an RMC is the only activity that would not. The correct answer is therefore (C).

stem: You are approached by a client with a minority shareholding in a private company. The client considers they are locked into the company which is being mismanaged by the major shareholders.
ask: Which of the following activities would a solicitor normally not need to perform in respect of recommending or arranging the sale of a client's shareholding in a private company, assuming an exemption applies under the SRA Financial Services (Scope) Rules 2001?

options.en: Inform the client in writing that the regulated activities carried on by the firm are limited in scope
Carry out the sale as soon as possible once the deal is agreed
Keep records of the client's instructions to effect the sale of the shares
Account to the client for any commission received from any third party in the course of the regulated activities
Provide the client with a copy of the Conduct of Business Rules

explanation.en: (A) - (D) are all requirements of the SRA Financial Services (Conduct of Business) Rules 2001. (E) is not required.

stem: You act for a client in a divorce settlement, which included the transfer of shares to the client. Your client now asks you for advice on selecting a suitable investment bond from among the many available in the financial market.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the above scenario?

options.en: An investment bond does not constitute a retail investment product
You can advise the client on the merits of investment bonds under certain circumstances
The client cannot be referred to an authorised person for independent advice in order to obtain the benefit of the 'introducing' exclusion under the RAO
An investment bond does not constitute a relevant investment
You are not permitted to give generic advice relating to the merits and demerits of investment bonds

explanation.en: (B) is the best option, because you are permitted to give generic advice relating to the merits and demerits of investment bonds (a particular class of investments) in general. Both option (A) and option (D) are not correct - an investment bond is both a security and a retail investment product. Option (C) is also untrue - because you cannot advise on the selection of a particular product, the only realistic way in which the advice can be given is te refer the client to an authorised person for independent advice.

stem: You act for a client in a divorce settlement which included the transfer of shares to the client. Arising out of your discussions with the client about her tax and legal affairs, and her need for cash, you advise her to sell some shares and agree to arrange their sale on her behalf, through a stockbroker.
ask: Which of the following statements is the most accurate in respect of the above scenario?

options.en: The general exclusion for 'necessary work' will apply here
If the arrangement for the sale is made on the client's specific instructions, a specific exclusion to the RAO will apply
If the arrangement for the sale is made on the client's specific instructions, a specific exclusion to the RAO will apply, but the sale must also be arranged with or through an authorised person
The work with the client cannot be said to be complementary to the matrimonial work done for the client, and so Part XX FSMA will not apply
No exclusion to the RAO will apply in this case

explanation.en: (C) is the best answer. Where the arrangement for the sale is made on the client's specific instructions and with or through an authorised person, i.e. on an execution-only basis, the arranging will be excluded from the RAO. (E) is not correct. The general exclusion for 'necessary work' is unlikely to apply here because the subsequent sale of shares is a new issue, separate from the divorce settlement itself - hence (A) is not accurate. If the arrangement cannot be considered execution-only because of the discussion with the client leading up to it, the Part XX general exemption should still apply because the work with the client 'arises out of' and is complementary to the matrimonial work done for the client (provided the provision of the financial service work is incidental to the provision of the professional service and that you account for all commission received from any third party). (D) is not, therefore, correct either.

stem: Your client has been awarded £100,000 in damages against the police for wrongful arrest, false imprisonment and malicious prosecution and currently seeks your advice as to what to do with the money. You have sufficient knowledge and experience of the investment options available, although you are not authorised by the FCA.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes the advice that you can provide?

options.en: The advice will not be regulated if it relates to the merits of buying or selling bank and building society deposit accounts
The advising is a necessary part of any other professional services you have rendered to your client
You would need FCA authorisation even if the advice is not given personally. You have to refer your client to an authorised person in order to receive independent advice
The Part XX exemption will apply to any advice you give on how best to invest the money
You would need FCA authorisation even if you refer your client to an authorised person in order to receive independent advice

explanation.en: (A) is the best answer. While deposit accounts are specified investments under the Act, they are not securities and are not, therefore, relevant investments. Moreover, the specified activity in relation to deposits under the Act is accepting - not advising. The advice in relation to deposit accounts will therefore not be regulated. (B) is false - the advising is not a necessary part of any other professional services you have rendered to the client, and the 'necessary' exclusion will not, therefore, apply. (D) is also false - because the money is separate from the award of damages, the complementary exemption will not, therefore, apply. The only way you could give specific advice would be to use an IFA - or, alternatively, to obtain authorisation from the FCA.

stem: You acted for the claimant in an action for the specific performance of a contract for the purchase of a minority holding of shares in a private company. The action was settled and the shares transferred by a stock transfer form which you prepared and lodged with the company's secretary.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes whether the arrangement was prohibited?

options.en: Preparing and lodging a transfer of shares does not constitute the regulated activity of arranging a deal for the sale of securities
Where the arrangements constitute an integral part of the settlement, they would be regulated activities under the RAO
Had the solicitor been required to advise the client on the purchase of the shares, such advice would not have been prohibited by Rule 5(3) of the Scope Rules
The arranging is not complementary to the main legal services being provided by the solicitor and will not constitute exempt regulated business under the Scope Rules
Had the solicitor been required to advise the client on the purchase of the shares, such advice would have been prohibited by Rule 5(3) of the Scope Rules

explanation.en: (C) is the best answer. Rule 5(3) of the Scope Rules prohibits advising a client to buy shares on an investment exchange. Here, however, the shares of a private company are being purchased, in which case the prohibition will not apply. Shares are a specified investment under the FSMA as well as securities. Preparing and lodging the transfer of securities is arranging - which constitutes a regulated activity under the RAO (hence (A) is incorrect). The necessary exclusion may apply here and, if not, the Part XX exemption will apply ((B), (D) and (E) are therefore incorrect).

stem: You are a high street firm with a strong local reputation. You are approached by life insurance agents. They suggest a reciprocal arrangement in which they would refer clients to you and you would recommend that clients use their services. The life insurance agents are tied agents.
ask: Which of the following best describes the requirements of the SRA Code of Conduct?

options.en: The SRA Code of Conduct prohibits the referral of a client to a tied agent in any circumstances
The SRA Code of Conduct prohibits the referral of a client to a tied life assurance agent generally speaking
The SRA Code of Conduct prohibits in all circumstances a solicitor to have an arrangement under which an introducer stipulates that the solicitor must sell only one particular mortgage
The SRA Code of Conduct permits the referral of a client to a tied agent, provided such referral is in the client's best interests and the requirements of the Code are complied with
The SRA Code of Conduct permits the referral of a client to a life insurance agent in any circumstances

explanation.en: The best answer is (D). (A) is not accurate: IB6.1 permits referrals to a tied agent (e.g. local estate agent or financial advisor), provided the solicitor ensures that he is not in breach of 01.2 and mandatory principle 4 (client's interest must precede your interests or any other third party's interests). (B) and (E) are inaccurate. A referral to a tied life insurance broker is only permitted under 06.3, if this is in the best interests of the client and the client is informed that the adviser is an appointed representative. (C) is also inaccurate, as there is no impediment in having an arrangement under which an introducer stipulates that you might sell only one particular mortgage, provided that it is suitable for the client's needs and you have informed the client of the constraint (IB6.1 and IB6.2).

stem: A solicitor successfully brokers a settlement for the specific performance of a contract in which his client will purchase a certain number of shares in the other side's company. His client now asks the solicitor to present the other party with a cheque on the client's behalf, draw up a stock transfer form and to submit the completed form to the company secretary to register the transfer of ownership.
ask: Which of the following best explains what the solicitor may do?

options.en: The solicitor may perform the activities that follow his negotiation of the settlement, because these form a necessary part of his negotiation services
The solicitor may perform the activities that follow his negotiation of the settlement, because these arise out of his negotiation services
The solicitor may not perform the activities that follow his negotiation of the settlement, because these are not complementary to his negotiation services
The solicitor may not perform the activities that follow his negotiation of the settlement, because these form the subject of a separate retainer
The solicitor may not perform the activities that follow his negotiation of the settlement, because these are all regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority

explanation.en: The most accurate answer is (B). The activities of presenting the other party with a cheque on behalf of his client, drawing up a stock transfer form and submitting the completed form to the company secretary for registration of the transfer of ownership would all constitute the regulated activity of arranging a deal under the FSMA. Moreover, the above activities might not reasonably be regarded as comprising a necessary part of the negotiation services (which would enable them to fall within 'the necessary exclusion' under the RAO). Nonetheless, the Part XX FSMA general exemption should apply, since the arrangements arise out of and are complementary to the provision of a professional service to the client (negotiation of a settlement), and the manner of providing the service will be incidental to the provision of the negotiation itself.

stem: You negotiate a settlement in a personal injury case in which your client will receive a lump-sum payment. The client now seeks your advice on how best to invest the money.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes what the solicitor may do?

options.en: The solicitor may not advise his client on how best to invest the money
The solicitor may advise his client on how best to invest the money, because such advice arises out of the litigation work that the solicitor has undertaken for the client
The solicitor may advise his client on how best to invest the money, because such advice is complementary to the litigation work that the solicitor has undertaken for the client
The solicitor may advise his client on how best to invest the money, because such advice is a necessary part of the other services that the solicitor has undertaken for the client
The solicitor may advise his client on how best to invest the money, because he is accounting to the client for the entire sum

explanation.en: The correct answer is (A). The investment advice is not a necessary party of the provision of the solicitor's negotiation services (which have already concluded) and nor would it arise out of or be complementary to the litigation work undertaken for the client!

stem: Messrs. Ford, Rolls and Bentley own 100% of the share capital in Fine Cars Ltd, a company which they founded (all of the shares carry equal voting rights). Ford owns 30% of the share capital, Rolls owns 30% and Bentley owns the remaining 40%. Mr. Ford wishes to sell his shares in the business to Mr. Rolls.
ask: Which of the following best explains the legal position?

options.en: The solicitor may act for Mr. Ford in the sale of his shares to Mr. Rolls because there is no specified investment activity involved in dealing with the sale
The solicitor may advise Mr. Ford in the sale of his shares to Mr. Rolls, but may not arrange for the execution of the sale, because arranging constitutes a specified investment activity
The solicitor may not act for Mr. Ford in the sale of his shares to Mr. Rolls because less than 50% of the voting shares in the company are being transferred
The solicitor may act for Mr. Ford in the sale of his shares to Mr. Rolls using the takeover (sale of body corporate) exclusion
The solicitor may act for Mr. Ford in the sale of his shares and for Mr. Rolls in the purchase of the shares from Mr. Ford

explanation.en: The solicitor cannot act for both Messrs. Ford and Rolls, due to the inherent conflict of interest between the two. He could, however, act for Mr. Ford alone. Dealing with the sale of the shares would involve the solicitor in negotiating, advising and/or arranging - all specified investment activities in respect of specified investments (the shares). The solicitor would therefore need to rely on an exclusion or exemption. The takeover (sale of body corporate) exclusion would appear, at first sight, not to apply in this case, because the transfer of shares does not include more than 50% of the voting shares in the company. However, the exclusion is also satisfied where the transfer will give Mr. Rolls more than 50% of the voting shares following the transfer, which would be the case here. Therefore, the correct answer is (D).

stem: A litigation partner in your firm is asked by a client to advise her on how she should invest £100,000 of damages recovered in a personal injury action. The client has no immediate need for the money. She tells the solicitor that she is considering investing in shares, property and works of art for maximum long term growth.
ask: Which of the following statements best describes what the solicitor may do?

options.en: The solicitor may advise the client regarding the purchase of the property and works of art, even though these constitute specified investments under the RAO.
The solicitor may advise the client regarding the purchase of the shares in a particular company
The solicitor may advise the client on what types of shares are available and how an investment can be made in shares

The solicitor may advise the client regarding the purchase of the shares in a particular company because the advice can reasonably be regarded as a necessary part of the solicitor's other professional services

The solicitor may advise the client regarding the purchase of the shares in a particular company because the advice is incidental to the litigation claim for which the solicitor was instructed by the client

explanation.en: The nest answer is C. Property and works of art are not specified investments for the purposes of the FSMA - and hence the second part of (A) is incorrect. Advising on the merits of a particular investment is prohibited, unless an exclusion or exemption applies. The 'necessary' exclusion would be unlikely to apply here, because the advice is not reasonably regarded as a necessary part of the solicitor's litigation services; indeed, the solicitor could easily refer the client to an IFA for this advice. Nor would the financial advice be incidental to the provision of the legal services provided to the client (moreover, rule 5(3) of the Scope Rules also provides that firms may not recommend an individual client to buy shares where the transaction will be made on a stock exchange, such as where the client is advised to invest in listed company shares). The only advice that can therefore be given with regard to the shares in generic advice - the solicitor could explain to the client what types of shares are available and how an investment can be made. Hence the correct answer is (C).

stem: You have many years of experience in investment and finance. You advise a broad spectrum of clients including entrepreneurs, executives and corporate officers. Your firm is carrying on non-mainstream regulated activities.
ask: Which of the following best describes the rules and regulations which the firm will need to comply with?

options.en: The Rule Book of the Financial Conduct Authority and the SRA Code of Conduct
The Rule Book of the Financial Conduct Authority, but not the SRA Code of Conduct
The Rule Book of the Financial Conduct Authority, the SRA Code of Conduct and the Money Laundering Regulations
The Rule Book of the Financial Conduct Authority, the SRA Code of Conduct, the SRA Conduct of Business Rules 2001 and the Money Laundering Regulations
The SRA Conduct of Business Rules 2001, the Money Laundering Regulations and the SRA Code of Conduct

explanation.en: The correct answer is (E). Solicitors need to comply with the FCA Rule Book where they are authorised by the FCA to carry out mainstream regulated activities. All solicitors are also required to comply with the SRA Code of Conduct and Money Laundering Regulations at all times. The SRA Financial Services (Conduct of Business Rules) 2001 (COB Rules) regulate the manner in which solicitors' firms should carry on regulated activities of the kind permitted by Part XX FSMA, which sets out a general exemption from the requirement to be regulated by the FCA for professional firms whose activities are incidental to their main professional business. While a breach of the COB Rules would not constitute a criminal offence, it could lead to disciplinary action by the SRA.

stem: You are a case worker for the SRA. The Financial Conduct Authority contacts the SRA to report a solicitor caught carrying on a regulated activity without obtaining appropriate authorisation from the Financial Conduct Authority. The solicitor admits responsibility but asserts that his advice was competent.
ask: Which of the following best describes what the consequences could be for the solicitor?

options.en: The solicitor could be imprisoned for up to two years but any agreement made in the course of carrying out the regulated activity would remain enforceable against the other party
The solicitor could be liable to a fine but any agreement made in the course of carrying out the regulated activity would remain enforceable against the other party
The solicitor could be liable to his own client in contract or tort, but any agreement made in the course of carrying out the regulated activity would remain enforceable against the other party
The solicitor could be liable to his own client in contract or tort, because any agreement made in the course of carrying out the regulated activity would be unenforceable against the other party
The solicitor could be reported to the Solicitors Regulation Authority, but could not be imprisoned or fined

explanation.en: The best answer is D. The consequences of carrying out a regulated activity without appropriate authorisation are that the solicitor could be sentenced to imprisonment for a maximum of 2 years and fined. Any agreement made in the course of carrying out a regulated activity in contravention of the general prohibition would be unenforceable against the other party (s. 26(1) FSMA). In addition, the other party could recover any money or property paid or transferred under the agreement and also compensation for any loss sustained as a result of parting with the money or property and this in turn could result in liability to one's client in contract or tort. The correct answer is therefore (D).

stem: Your client tells you that he wants to buy a house, but has no idea what type of mortgage to take out. You would like to introduce the client to a particular mortgage provider with whom you regularly work and who refers clients to the solicitor from time to time.
ask: Which of the following best explains the legal position?

options.en: The solicitor may introduce the client to the particular mortgage provider with whom he regularly works
The solicitor may introduce the client to the particular mortgage provider with whom he regularly works even if the introducer sells only one particular mortgage package
The solicitor may introduce the client to the particular mortgage provider with whom he regularly works provided that the introducer does not sell only one particular mortgage package
The solicitor may not introduce the client to the particular mortgage provider with whom he regularly works because this constitutes a restrictive arrangement
The solicitor may not introduce the client to the particular mortgage provider because it is not in the client's best interest to be referred to a tied agent

explanation.en: The best answer is B. 06.1 of the SRA Code of Conduct prevents entering into restrictive arrangements in general in connection with regulated activities that could constrain the advice a solicitor give to his clients or the referrals that he makes. However, the prohibition on entering into a restrictive arrangement does not apply to arrangements in connection with regulated mortgage contracts (IB6.1). This means that a solicitor would not be prevented from having an arrangement under which an introducer stipulates that he might only sell one particular mortgage policy, provided that it is suitable for the client's needs and he has informed the client of the constraint (IB6.2). In the case in question, the introducer is not a tied agent. While a restrictive arrangement exists between the solicitor and the introducer, this is acceptable as explained above. Therefore, the correct answer is (B).

stem: A solicitor refers a client to a financial advisor who is the appointed representative of a large building society. The advisor is requested to advise on the purchase of some unit trusts in a fund managed by the building society. The purchase is subsequently made on the client's behalf by the financial advisor.
ask: Which of the following best explains the legal position?

options.en: The solicitor's referral to the financial advisor is made on an execution-only basis because the purchase of the unit trusts is made by the financial advisor
The solicitor's referral to the financial advisor satisfies the incidental exemption to the regulated activity of arranging
The solicitor's referral to the financial advisor is in order because it is in the client's best interests
The solicitor's referral to the financial advisor is a referral to an authorised third person and thus constitutes an exclusion to the regulated activity of arranging
The solicitor's referral to the financial advisor does not constitute a referral for independent advice

explanation.en: The solicitor's referral to the financial advisor is not an independent referral. In addition, the appointed representative will not be an authorised person, but an exempt person. There is therefore no (authorised third person) exclusion to arranging, and the solicitor has carried out an unauthorised investment activity. The solicitor has also breached mandatory principle 4, 01.2 and 06.1 of the Code of Conduct by not acting in the client's best interests. Therefore, the correct answer is (E).

stem: Your firm, Oliver, Dickens & Co. provides private client advice to high value individuals which includes setting up offshore trusts and investing assets. You advise about and arrange purchase and disposal of euros, cash ISAs, premium bonds and national savings certificates. The client requests that you also acquire company preference shares, ordinary share warrants, futures for investment gain, government stock and local authority bonds.
ask: Which of the following best represents the firm's additional obligations if it accepts these instructions?

options.en: You have already been providing advice listed in the Regulated Activities Order 2001 and so there will be no change
will need to become authorised by the FCA or rely on an exemption since the new activities, as opposed to the existing ones, are listed in the Regulated Activities Order
You will need to become authorised by the FCA whether or not the new activities, or the existing ones, are listed in the Regulated Activities Order 2001
You do not need to become authorised by the FCA or rely on an exemption since the activities are not listed in the Regulated Activities Order 2001
You do not need to become authorised by the FCA or rely on an exemption since the activities are listed in the Regulated Activities Order 2001

explanation.en: The correct answer is (B). Activities listed in the Regulated Activities Order 2001 (RAO) are regulated under the FSMA and require authorisation or exemption. This includes advising about company preference shares, ordinary share warrants, futures for investment gain, government stock and local authority bonds. Euros, cash ISAs, premium bonds and national savings certificates are not listed as regulated investments under the RAO. A Is not correct, as Euros, cash ISAs, premium bonds and national savings certificates are not listed as regulated investments under the RAO. C is not correct as authorisation or exemption is only required in respect of regulated activities. D is not correct. Advising about company preference shares, ordinary share warrants, futures for investment gain, government stock and local authority bonds are regulated activities and you would need to become authorised by the FCA or rely on an exemption. E is not correct. You do need to become authorised by the FCA or rely on an exemption if you carry out regulated activities. Failure to do so is a criminal offence under section 19 FSMA, contracts arranged will be unenforceable and failure to comply with statutory obligations is also a regulatory offence (07.5).

stem: You are a partner in a large global firm, Cliffields & May. At a dinner party, you recommend to friends and family that they should invest in shares in India Investment Trust plc. India Investment Trust plc. are not clients of yours and you do not have insider information. The advice involves no confidential information.
ask: Which of the following best describes you position under the FSMA?

options.en: You are likely to have breached the FSMA unless your firm was authorised
You are likely to have breached the ESMA unless you can rely on the exemption for professionals
You did not breach the FSMA because your advice did not constitute a business activity, as it was made in a non-business capacity
You did not breach the FSMA because your advice did not constitute a business activity and so you can rely on the exemption for professionals
If you were authorised you would not be in breach of the FSMA, because your advice did not constitute a business activity, as it was made in a non-business capacity

explanation.en: The best answer is C. Firms are not required to obtain FCA authorisation or rely on an exemption under the FSMA if they do not provide advice about regulated investments in a non-business context. If the dinner party was in fact a business meeting, the FSMA restrictions would apply. A is not correct as advice in a non-business context does not require FCA authorisation. B is not correct as exemption is not required for advice in a non-business context. D is not correct as exemption is not required for advice in a non-business context. Exemption applies when advice is given in a business context. E is not correct as authorisation is not required for advice in a non-business context. FCA authorisation is only required when advice is given in a business context.

stem: Your firm is not authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority. It wishes to make arrangements for Mrs Montefiore, a probate client, to buy and sell some unit trusts. You make the arrangements following the advice of an authorised third person. The shares subsequently rise in value and Mrs Montefiore misses out on a large profit that she could have made.
ask: Which of the following best describes the position under the FSMA?

options.en: As the advice was given following the advice of an ATP, you were not in breach of the ESMA
It makes no difference that the advice was made following the advice of an ATP, but you could rely on the execution-only client exclusion
You are likely to have been in breach of the FSMA, even though the advice was given following the advice of an ATP
You are likely to have been in breach of the FSMA, unless you could rely on the execution-only client exclusion
As the advice was made following the advice of an ATP, you could rely on the execution-only client exclusion

explanation.en: A is the best answer. You can rely on the ATP exemption (Article 29 RAO) and would not be in breach of the FSMA. You do not need to rely on the execution-only exclusion. B is not the best answer. You may be able to rely on the execution-only exclusion but you can rely on the ATP exception. You can probably rely on the ATP exemption. C is not correct. You can probably rely on the ATP exemption. D is not the best answer. You can rely on the ATP exemption and would not be in breach of the FSMA. You do not need to rely on the execution-only exclusion. E is not the best answer. You do not need the advice on an ATP to rely on the execution-only exception. You can probably rely on the ATP exemption in any event and do not need to rely on the execution-only exception.

stem: Your client, Sharmoun, is buying a house and has decided on an endowment mortgage. Sharmoun instructs you to get a quote for a life policy from Imprudent Insurance plc., and to complete the application form. You are not authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority but often provide incidental mortgage advice in property transaction.
ask: Which of the following best represents whether you can fulfil the client's instructions?

options.en: You can carry out the request without FCA authorisation
You cannot carry out the request without FCA authorisation
You can obtain the quote without FCA authorisation but need authorisation to complete the application form
You need FCA authorisation to obtain the quote but do not need authorisation to complete the application form
You can carry out the request without FCA authorisation, relying on the introducing or authorised third party exception

explanation.en: (B) is the correct answer. Obtaining a quote and completing the application form in respect of the endowment life policy would be 'arranging' within the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000. Under Article 33 of the RAO, on the facts described above, a solicitor would be forbidden to introduce a client even to an independent financial advisor (and in this case Imprudent Insurance may not even be able to give him independent advice); this is because the "introducing" and "ATP" exclusions do not apply to insurance mediation activities. Moreover, completing an application form and/or sending it to the insurance provider may not even fall within the limited exclusion contained in Article 72C (provision of information on an incidental basis). (A) is not correct. You require authorisation for both activities. (C) is not correct. Obtaining a quote in respect of the endowment life policy would also be 'arranging' within the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (although if carried out without filling out forms, it could have qualified for an exclusion under Article 72C as being on an incidental basis). (D) is not correct. Completing the application form in respect of the endowment life policy would also be 'arranging' within the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000. (E) is not correct. Under Article 33 of the RAO, a solicitor is forbidden to introduce a client even to an independent financial advisor because the "introducing" and "ATP" exclusions do not apply to insurance mediation activities.

stem: Your firm acts for the trustees of Jackson, deceased. The trust fund is invested in suitable stocks and shares. Your firm receives dividends. The personal representatives subsequently instruct the firm to re-organise the portfolio. They do not ask the firm to exercise its discretion as to which investments to make. All the routine decisions will be taken by an authorised financial adviser.
ask: Which of the following best represents the firm's position regarding authorisation?

options.en: The firm could be arranging, managing and safeguarding investments. They cannot rely on an exception and must be authorised by the FCA
The firm could be advising and safeguarding investments. They can rely on the trustee exemption
The firm could be arranging and safeguarding investments. As they have no discretion, they do not have to be authorised by the FCA
The firm could be arranging, managing and safeguarding investments. They can rely on the trustee exemption and would not require FCA authorisation
The only activity involved is safeguarding investments. This is likely to come under the necessary exemption

explanation.en: (C) is the best answer. The firm could be arranging and safeguarding investments. If the only activity involved is receiving dividends - then the only relevant investment activity could be safeguarding. Where, however, the firm is asked to restructure the investment portfolio, it may be advising and arranging too (for example, if it gives advice to the trustees, who then take that advice and instruct the firm to arrange for some shares to be sold and others bought). The firm would be managing if the trustees actually instruct the firm to make the decision as to which shares should be bought and sold (however, only if there is discretion vested in the firm will re-organising the portfolio actually constitute "managing"). Possible exclusions include: where the safeguarding forms a reasonably necessary part of the trust work; where the ATP or the execution-only client exclusions are used to carry out the advising and arranging; where no discretion is involved in the management of the investments or a power of attorney is appointed to manage the investments under which all the routine decisions are taken either by an authorised or exempt person. (A) is not correct. The firm would be managing if the trustees actually instruct the firm to make the decision as to which shares should be bought and sold i.e. if they have some discretion. (B) is not the best answer. The trustee exclusion will not be available to the firm - because the firm merely acts for the trustees, and not in the capacity of trustees. (D) is not the best answer. The trustee exclusion will not be available to the firm - because the firm merely acts for the trustees, and not in the capacity of trustees. (E) is not the best answer. Although safeguarding is likely to be necessary, it is unlikely that arranging would benefit from this exclusion. However, the ATP, execution-only or absence of discretion would likely apply and FCA authorisation would probably not be required.

stem: You act for Fred and Wilma, who have been awarded substantial damages. They ask you to advise on how best to invest the damages. They are considering investing the money in company shares. They ask you whether the Bedrock Mining Company is a sound investment and which other companies you would recommend investing in.
ask: Which of the following best represents your position under the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000?

options.en: You would be advising under the Act. You would need authorisation or an exemption
You are not advising under the Act and do not need authorisation or exemption
You would be advising under the Act if you provide generic advice, and should refer the clients to an authorised third person
You would be advising under the Act if you provide advice about specific companies, and should refer the clients to an authorised third person
You would be exempt under the Act if you provide generic advice, but not if you provide specific advice

explanation.en: (D) is best answer. Generic advice - to explain in general the advantages and disadvantages of all types of investment - does not constitute 'advising' within the Act: unit trusts as against investment trusts, building society accounts with company shares. However, any advice you give as to which particular company the client should invest in will constitute specific advice and will be caught by the Act. The appropriate way to avoid the 'advising' activity would be to decline to give Fred and Wilma advice and recommend that they take independent financial advice before reaching a decision via an authorised third person (Article 29 RAO). A is not the best answer. If you only provide generic advice or refer the clients to an authorised third person, you do not require authorisation or exemption. B is not the best answer. If you provide specific advice you would be advising and would require authorisation or an exception such as the ATP exception. C is not correct. If you provide generic advice only, you would not be advising under the Act and do not need to rely on the ATP exception. E is not the best answer. Generic advice is not exempt under the Act. It is not covered by the Act. Specific advice may be subject to an exception such as the ATP exception. There is no need to be authorised to give generic advice, even if no other exception applies.

stem: Your client, Donoghue McAllister, is purchasing a house. She asks you to advise about mortgages. You are authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority, but intend to act in your role as a solicitor, not as a separate business. You decide to refer the client to Home Sweet Home Mortgage Services who only provide Barcloyds of Scotland mortgages.
ask: Which of the following best summarizes the professional conduct implications?

options.en: A referral should be made to an independent financial adviser, unless you are sure Home Sweet Home will provide the best terms
You cannot regularly refer clients to Home Sweet Home. You must find an independent financial adviser or advise the client to appoint their own intermediary
You cannot refer the client to an independent financial adviser
You can refer the client to Home Sweet Home Mortgage Services
